High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:194155
Court No. - 84
Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 4618 of 2024
Revisionist :- Juvenile X
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Revisionist :- Ramesh Chandra Yadav

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.

1-The present criminal revision under Section 102 of Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 has been preferred against the judgment and order dated 16.08.2024 passed by learned Additional District and Sessions Judge/Special Judge (POCSO Act), Jalaun at Orai in Criminal Appeal No. 47 of 2024 (Vinit Kumar vs. State of U.P.) and against order dated 30.07.2024 passed by Juvenile Justice Board, Jalaun at Orai in Case No. 27 of 2024 arising out of Case Crime No. 90 of 2024, under Sections 363, 366, 376 I.P.C. and Sections 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Kuthaund, District Jalaun whereby the learned Juvenile Justice Board as well as learned appellate court refused the prayer of bail of accused-revisionist.
2-Despite service of notice upon the complainant/informant, no one has put in appearance on his behalf.

entities.label: STATUTE

entities.label: COURT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence this Court proceeds to hear this matter on merit.

Juvenile X vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117415508/
1 3-Heard learned counsel for the revisionist and learned Additional Government Advocate representing the State of U.P. and perused the record.
4-As per the prosecution case in brief, complainant-Rambabu Rathore who is father of the victim lodged a first information report on 17.04.2024 for the offence under Section 366 I.P.C. against unknown person alleging inter-alia that on 16.04.2024 at about 04:00 o'clock, his daughter was enticed away by unknown person with whom she was having telephonic conversation on his mobile phone number 9569437608.
5-Learned counsel for the revisionist, assailing the impugned orders, submits that the revisionist was a juvenile on the date of the alleged incident dated 16.04.2024 and he has been declared juvenile vide order dated 05.07.2024 of Juvenile Justice Board treating the age of revisionist as 16 years, 09 months and 15 days on the date of alleged incident.

entities.text: Juvenile X vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is next submitted that aforesaid order declaring the revisionist as juvenile has attained finality because the same has not been challenged by the informant, the averment in this regard has been made in para no. 3 of the supplementary affidavit dated 04.12.2024.

So far as the mobile number, as mentioned in the F.I.R.
is concerned, it is argued that the sim card was in the name of one Kapil and was being used by the revisionist for telephonic conversation with the victim on account of love affair with her.
The revisionist has remained confined in juvenile home since 14.05.2024.
6-As to the offence alleged, it is submitted that the revisionist has falsely been implicated in the case with ulterior motive.
In this regard, it is further stated that proper investigation was not conducted by the police and thus the revisionist had wrongly been charged with the offence.
The revisionist is not named in the F.I.R.

Referring the statement of the victim under Section 164 Cr.P.C., it is next argued that the victim has stated inter-alia that she was inclined to marry with the revisionist and since her parents were not ready for this relation, therefore, they scolded and assaulted her as a result whereof, victim herself left her house on 16.04.2024 and she, after solemnizing marriage with the revisionist, went to Bulandshahr.
The victim has also not supported the prosecution case.
7-It is further being emphasized that the revisionist does not have any criminal antecedent to his credit.

Lastly, it is submitted that there is no material on record for believing that the release of revisionist is likely to bring him into association with any known criminal or expose him to moral,
psychological danger, therefore, aforesaid impugned orders are not sustainable and liable to be set aside and revisionist is entitled to be released on bail in view of Section 12 of Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Child) Act, 2015.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Child) Act, 2015
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 8-Learned Additional Government Advocate vehemently opposed the present revision.
It has thus been submitted, merely because the revisionist is a juvenile it would not entitle him to bail without going into the gravity of the offence, the nature of the crime.
It is also contended that the bail sought for has been rightly refused in view of Section 12(1) of Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Child) Act, 2015.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Child) Act, 2015
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 9-Having considered the arguments so advanced by learned counsel for the parties, I find that there is no adverse report of District Probation Officer, Jalaun against the revisionist.

This Court also Juvenile X vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117415508/
2 finds that the victim, in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. has clearly stated that the revisionist did not commit any misdeed with her and she herself left her house and want to live with the revisionist.

entities.text: Juvenile X vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10-The Court has to see whether the opinion of the learned appellate Court as well as Juvenile Justice Board recorded in the impugned judgment and orders are in consonance with the provision of Section 12 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Section 12 of the aforesaid Act lays down three contingencies in which bail could be refused to juvenile.

They are:-
(i) if the release is likely to bring him into association with any known criminal, or (ii) expose him to moral, physical or psychological danger, or (iii) that his release would defeat the ends of justice.
11-Considering the facts of the case as noted above, it appears that the findings recorded by the learned Court below are erroneous and cannot be sustained.
The aforesaid impugned orders dated 16.08.2024 and 30.07.2024 are hereby set aside.
12-Accordingly, the present criminal revision is allowed.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law;
(iii) The revisionist through guardian shall remain present before the trial Court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.

In case of his absence,
without sufficient cause, the trial Court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

13-Let the revisionist Juvenile X, involved in the aforesaid case crime be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond of his father, namely, Girja Shankar who is his natural guardian with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-

(ii) The revisionist through guardian shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the date fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
